_comment: MotionLab thresholds. Every detector reads its section here; tune values, then re-run analyze.py with --redetect (re-uses cached per-frame metrics, no re-decode). Units: luma/sat in %, motion in % of frame width (x) / height (y) per frame, scale as ratio per frame, rotation in degrees per frame, RGB shift in source pixels.

cut._comment: hard cut = one-frame content change. rel = value / local median. corr = structure correlation with the previous frame (only trusted when both thumbnails have contrast >= min_thumb_std, otherwise the frame-difference ratio fd_rel_min is used).

flash._comment: flash = short luma spike. luma_delta = rise in luma % over 1-2 frames; white = whole frame >= white_luma with p05 >= white_p05. look_* = the measured 'flash look' (evidence only, types unchanged): the area brighter than the frame before the flash by > look_diff_min levels (0-255, at the extract width); texture below look_flat_texture = a flat solid frame, above = an over-exposed picture that keeps its texture (4AM: flat 0.3-1.2, textured 3.8-23).

transition._comment: gradual transitions. stride = frames compared on each side (t-stride vs t+stride); lo/hi = progress thresholds that mark the first/last affected frame; spread = spatial spread of per-pixel progress at the midpoint (dissolve: every pixel at the same progress, low spread; wipe/iris/luma fade: some areas already switched, high spread); same_picture_corr = above this the picture did not change (colour/brightness change only, not a shot transition).

near_miss._comment: possible misses listed for the user / reviewer (evidence only, never events): local peaks of the same surprise score as 'unknown' (robust z of luma / saturation / colour / picture change) from z_min up that no event (+- pad_frames) and no cut explains; at most max_items, spacing_frames apart.
